constraints:
# KBD Constraints

Constraints the artifact-refiner QA gate validates for every change from
`phase-codex-plugin-distribution-and-ci` onward. Each completed change is checked
against these before archiving (`/refine-validate <change-id>`); a violation marks
the change BLOCKED.

## C-01 — Generated artifacts must be in sync

Any source consumed by a generator must have its generated outputs regenerated
and committed before the owning parent phase completes or its final phase
commit is pushed. A parent phase may name one later reconciliation change to batch this
work when several sibling changes edit the same generated surface; every earlier
change must identify that reconciliation change in persisted execution evidence,
and none may claim distribution certification in the interim. The reconciliation
change must run the generator twice, prove byte-identical tracked hashes, and run
the applicable drift validators before phase certification. A deferral that
crosses the parent-phase boundary, omits the named owner, or reaches parent-phase
certification, final commit, or push without regenerated outputs is a violation.

Also generator inputs, from the integration contract (v1.0.0) onward:
`shared/launchagents/*.plist` and `shared/systemd/*.service|.timer|.path` feed
`shared/services.manifest.json` via `scripts/generate-service-manifest.mjs`
(seam 3 of `docs/integration-contract.md`). Any change that edits, adds, or
deletes one of those templates MUST regenerate the manifest and pass
`npm run check:services-manifest` in the same change. The manifest is generated;
hand-editing it is a violation.

Specifically: after touching `.claude-plugin/*`, `.mcp.json`,
`hooks/hooks.json`, or `scripts/build-codex-plugin.js`, `npm run validate:codex`
MUST pass (no drift, valid manifest + marketplace) in the same change because
those files directly define the generator or already-generated plugin surface.
Hand-editing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` or
`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is always a violation — they are generated.

## C-02 — No committed secrets

No API keys, tokens, or passwords in tracked files. Env vars and `${VAR:-default}`
placeholders only; real secret values live in the environment or user-local config
(`~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.bash_profile`), never in the repo. Localhost dev
credentials that are already an established repo convention (e.g. surrealdb
`root/root`, the forge localhost dev token) are exempt.

## C-03 — Docs updated with surface changes

A change that alters the Codex plugin surface (manifest fields, marketplace
schema, MCP servers, hooks, install flow) must update `docs/codex-plugin.md` and,
where relevant, the CLAUDE.md "Codex CLI Integration" section in the same change.

## C-04 — Generators stay idempotent

`node scripts/build-codex-plugin.js` run twice must produce byte-identical output.
`--check` must exit non-zero on drift or invalid artifacts. New generator features
(e.g. source-type knobs) must preserve idempotency for a fixed input.

## C-05 — Scripts under launchd are bash 3.2 compatible

Any script that can be invoked by a launchd agent (macOS `/bin/bash` is 3.2) must
avoid `mapfile` / `declare -A`. Test with `/bin/bash script.sh`, not just `bash`.

## QA and local review coverage

Every change requires deterministic artifact validation followed by independent
cumulative diff review before archive and final certification, including small
and documentation-only changes. Missing tools or explicit skip flags record
`pending_review`; they do not imply a passing gate. Final certification requires
a completed review receipt or the explicit signed waiver required by the current
`kbd-execute` contract. Generated-output deferral is limited to C-01 above.

===== plan.md =====
# Plan — vlbv-r4-portability

Contract: `adopted-contract.json` (v2, 10 scenarios, lint clean; not yet adopted).
Method: VLBV. Every task below is implemented before the single B4 run; nothing
executes generated code earlier (D1). LSP diagnostics are static reading (D5).

## Tasks

| Task | Deliverable | Scenarios |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `evals/vlbv-protocol/cases/*.json`: 23 cases (AT 01–22 + §18). Each has an id, AT text reference, a classification (`agent` or `machinery`), the prompt/fixture, expected behaviour, and a deterministic check where one exists (file effects, forbidden commands in transcript) plus a grader rubric line for free-text judgement. A schema plus `scripts/check-skill-evals.js`-style shape check. | EVAL-* |
| T2 | `evals/vlbv-protocol/run.mjs` + `adapters/<harness>.mjs`. Per run: create a scratch project (`kbd-init`, installed pack generation), a scratch HOME and harness home, and copy the minimum auth file (claude: keychain is per-user so HOME relocation must be verified; codex: `auth.json`; opencode/kimi/qwen: their documented auth files). Hash real harness homes and the login-keychain item listing (attributes only) before and after. Capture transcripts and file effects under `evals/runs/<harness>/<case>/<sample>/`. Delete scratch, verify no auth leftovers. `--keep-scratch`/`--expect-leftover` for the negative control. Bash-free Node so it runs on launchd/bash 3.2 hosts. | EVAL-CLAUDE..QWEN-1, AUTH-ISO-1 |
| T3 | `evals/vlbv-protocol/grade.mjs` + `validate-report.mjs`. Cross-model grading through liter-llm (`kbd_complete`-equivalent REST), family-aware grader choice, 3 fixed samples, all retained. Reports `evals/reports/<harness>.{json,md}` with per-case k-of-3, pass/fail/not-run counts, transcript digests, grader identity. Machinery verdicts merged as `harness-independent`. Uninstalled harnesses → the 17 agent cases NOT_EXERCISED with reason, plus the shared machinery verdicts. Report validation rejects a PASS citing a missing transcript (negative control). Reports are scanned for secrets before writing (AT 22). | EVAL-*, EVAL-NOTRUN-1 |
| T4 | `evals/vlbv-protocol/machinery.mjs`: drive the real `kbd-phase-close-eval.sh`, `kbd-closure-packet.mjs` and the KBD runtime in a scratch project for AT 05, 06, 09, 10, 15, 22, plus `--negative --at ATnn` for each of the six ATs: that AT's trigger is removed and the real script must accept. | EVAL-MACH-1 |
| T5 | `evals/vlbv-protocol/apply-capabilities.mjs`: move a `capabilities.json` field to `supported` only from report evidence whose case declares that capability field (field-to-case linkage in the corpus) (exercised, date, version, evidence path); leave every other field unchanged. `--negative` writes a copy with an unexercised `supported` and expects `validate:harness-adapters` to reject it. | CAP-UPDATE-1 |
| T6 | CR-33. (a) Record an immutable B4 authorization event in the phase (`boundary-authorization.json`: timestamp, contract digest, authorizer), written when the boundary is authorized and before the first attempt; `value-scenario-verify`/`boundaries.md` say so. (b) `kbd-phase-close-eval.sh` scans `boundaryPacket.runnerOutputGlobs` and passes artifacts with mtime earlier than the event to `kbd-closure-packet.mjs`, which writes `preAuthorizationArtifacts[]` and a "Pre-authorization runner artifacts" section ("none found" when empty; "no authorization event recorded" when absent — never silent). (c) Schema: add `runnerOutputGlobs` to the v2 `boundaryPacket`. (d) `scan-fixture.mjs` builds the mixed and all-after fixtures. Report only; no guard. | SCAN-PRE-1 |

## Order

0. **Adopt the v2 contract** through `kbd-contract-adopt.sh` (digest per `digestNormalization`, planRevision pinned, phase bound). T1–T6 are blocked until the adoption decision is recorded.

Then T1 → T4 → T2 → T3 → T5 → T6, then documentation (vlbv skill references, CHANGELOG
Unreleased), then B4 authorization (owner) → the boundary packet once.

## Boundary packet

As declared in the contract: 26 commands, `singleRun`, machinery cases first (their verdicts feed every report), stop on AUTH-ISO-1 FAIL before any further harness; negative controls write only under `evals/reports/_negative/`. Expected spend: 255 agent harness sessions (17 × 3 × 5) plus grading; the 6 machinery cases run once (owner decision D-R4-03).

## Risks carried

R1 auth-in-isolation per harness (Claude Code's keychain login may not follow a
relocated HOME), R2 OpenCode isolation, R3 cost, R4 grader independence, R5
unrelated dirty `.kbd-orchestrator` projections kept out of commits.

# Goals

Owner-adopted scope (R4 of the VLBV change register, 2026-11-16).

- CR-31: add protocol evals under `evals/` that run VLBV acceptance tests AT 01-22 and the section 18 fresh-session check as cases against each harness capability profile. Installed harnesses: claude-code, codex, opencode, kimi, qwen-code. zed, minimax-code and mimo-code are reported not-run unless exercisable.
- CR-31 exit: one eval report per harness with pass, fail and not-run counts. A `capabilities.json` value moves to `supported` only with exercised evidence (FR-H7); unknown capabilities are listed, never assumed.
- CR-33: `kbd-phase-close-eval.sh` lists runner output artifacts dated before boundary authorization in the closure packet, or states that none were found. Report only, no tool guard (CF-36).
- Adopt a v2 contract before any generation (the first live v2 adoption). Implement completely before the single B4 boundary run. Unit tests are not evidence.

prior_round_findings.claim: The plan's Order never includes the v2 contract adoption step that the goals mandate before any generation, so the boundary packet would be run from an unadopted contract with a null digest.
prior_round_findings.evidence: Goals: "Adopt a v2 contract before any generation (the first live v2 adoption)." Plan header: "Contract: `adopted-contract.json` (v2, 10 scenarios, lint clean; not yet adopted)" and the Order section: "T1 → T4 → T2 → T3 → T5 → T6, then documentation (vlbv skill references, CHANGELOG Unreleased), then B4 authorization (owner) → the boundary packet once." — no adoption step exists anywhere in the Order, and the contract carries "contractDigest": null with "planRevision": null, so the digestNormalization stalenessRule ("digest mismatch against the latest non-superseded adoption decision") has no adoption decision to anchor to.
prior_round_findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit pre-T1 step in the Order: record the v2 adoption decision (digest computed per digestNormalization, planRevision pinned), and state that T1–T6 are blocked until it is recorded.

prior_round_findings.claim: EVAL-MACH-1's single negative control proves conditionality only for AT 06, so an implementation whose close-eval/closure/sanitization paths always refuse would still pass the refusal-shaped checks for AT 05, 09, 10, 15 and 22.
prior_round_findings.evidence: Comparator: "For each AT the real script produces the refusal/rejection the AT requires" — but negativeControl input is only "AT 06 fixture with the assertion present and passing" (commandRef neg-machinery-1, one command). Plan T4's corresponding text is equally singular and ambiguous: "plus a `--negative` mode where the AT condition is removed and the script must accept." Nothing in the scenarioMatrix or boundaryPacket removes the trigger condition for AT 05, 09, 10, 15 or 22.
prior_round_findings.suggested_fix: Make neg-machinery-1 per-AT: for each of the six machinery ATs, remove that AT's trigger condition and require the real script to accept; state this explicitly in T4 so the boundary command exercises all six negatives.

prior_round_findings.claim: The per-harness report comparator demands 'exactly 3 samples' for all 23 cases, which contradicts the run-machinery-once design: a truthful harness report with 1-sample machinery verdicts fails validation, while the wrong implementation (machinery re-run 3x per harness, or fabricated sample counts) passes — and the plan's 'about 345 harness sessions' spend figure encodes exactly that wrong assumption.
prior_round_findings.evidence: Every EVAL-*-1 comparator: "Report is accepted when: 23 cases present; each has exactly 3 samples or an explicit BLOCKED/NOT_EXERCISED reason" vs EVAL-MACH-1 scopeRefs: "Machinery cases executed once and counted in every report" and usefulOutcome "injected into every harness report as harness-independent". A merged machinery case has 1 sample and is neither BLOCKED nor NOT_EXERCISED, so it satisfies no arm of the comparator. 345 = 23 cases x 3 samples x 5 harnesses, but the declared design yields 17 x 3 x 5 = 255 agent sessions + 6 machinery runs, so the spend basis stated in the plan and in requiredApprovals ("about 345 harness sessions plus grading (D-R4-03)") double-counts machinery by ~90 sessions.
prior_round_findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the comparator to: 23 cases present; the 17 agent cases have exactly 3 samples or an explicit BLOCKED/NOT_EXERCISED reason; the 6 machinery cases carry the single harness-independent verdict; and recompute the D-R4-03 spend figure from 17x3x5 + 6.

prior_round_findings.claim: EVAL-MACH-1 and EVAL-NOTRUN-1 impose contradictory requirements on the zed/minimax-code/mimo-code reports: machinery verdicts must appear in 'every harness report', yet the not-run comparator requires all 23 cases NOT_EXERCISED with zero PASS.
prior_round_findings.evidence: EVAL-MACH-1: "injected into every harness report as harness-independent" with comparator "each harness report carries identical machinery verdicts"; EVAL-NOTRUN-1 comparator: "23 cases each NOT_EXERCISED with a reason naming the missing CLI; zero PASS". If machinery verdicts (which can be PASS) are injected into the not-run reports, 'zero PASS' fails; if they are not, 'every harness report' fails. Reporting the 6 harness-independent machinery cases as blocked on a missing CLI is also factually false.
prior_round_findings.suggested_fix: Scope EVAL-MACH-1's injection to the five installed-harness reports and change EVAL-NOTRUN-1's comparator to 'the 17 agent cases NOT_EXERCISED with a reason naming the missing CLI; the 6 machinery cases carry the shared machinery verdicts; zero agent PASS'.

prior_round_findings.claim: AUTH-ISO-1's file-manifest oracle cannot observe claude-code's macOS Keychain credential store, so an eval run that mutates real keychain state still passes 'manifests identical', and the negative control only proves detection of file leftovers.
prior_round_findings.evidence: AUTH-ISO-1 oracle: "Before/after SHA-256 manifest of real harness config and auth files; search of scratch root and repo for auth file names" with limitation "Covers files the runner knows about"; plan T2 concedes "claude: keychain is per-user so HOME relocation must be verified" and risk R1 is "Claude Code's keychain login may not follow a relocated HOME". Keychain writes (e.g. token refresh during the 69 claude-code sessions) are invisible to a file-hash manifest, and neg-iso-1 (--keep-scratch/--expect-leftover) exercises only the file-leftover path.
prior_round_findings.suggested_fix: Extend the AUTH-ISO-1 oracle for claude-code with a keychain-observable check (e.g. `security dump-keychain` item-count/listing hash before and after) or explicitly declare keychain mutation as out of observable scope in the scenario limitations.

prior_round_findings.claim: The neg-iso-1 boundary command re-invokes run.mjs for claude-code with the same report output path as EVAL-CLAUDE-1, so in the singleRun packet it can clobber the accepted claude-code report that cap-apply and the receipts depend on.
prior_round_findings.evidence: neg-iso-1 argv: ["node","evals/vlbv-protocol/run.mjs","--harness","claude-code","--samples","1","--keep-scratch","--expect-leftover"]; plan T3: "Reports `evals/reports/<harness>.{json,md}`"; boundaryPacket receipts: ["boundary-results.json","evals/reports/"] and runnerOutputGlobs ["evals/reports/**","evals/runs/**"]. Nothing in the contract or plan states the negative-control run writes to a separate report path, and it runs (command 20) after eval-claude-code (command 1) in a packet declared singleRun.
prior_round_findings.suggested_fix: Route negative-control runs to a quarantine path (e.g. evals/reports/_negative/ or require --expect-leftover to imply --report-dir) and state that evals/reports/claude-code.json is written exactly once.

prior_round_findings.claim: CAP-UPDATE-1's oracle checks only that an evidence path exists, not that the evidence corresponds to the capability field it is cited for, so a wrong evidence-to-capability mapping passes validation.
prior_round_findings.evidence: Comparator: "Every field changed to supported has verified.exercised true and an evidence path that exists"; negativeControl input is only "A capabilities.json copy with one field set supported and no exercised evidence". An apply-capabilities.mjs that marks capability X supported while citing capability Y's (existing) report evidence satisfies both the comparator and the negative control, and 'no field without report evidence changes' is not mechanically defined.
prior_round_findings.suggested_fix: Require the validator to resolve each cited evidence path to the case/harness whose report actually exercised that capability (field-to-case linkage declared in the case corpus), and add a negative control with a valid-but-mismatched evidence path.
